questions.q: What is identity, according to Taylor?
questions.a: A person's understanding of who they are
w: A person's position in society
The way a person dresses
The laws and traditions of a country

questions.q: How is a person's identity partly shaped?
questions.a: By recognition and the opinions of others
w: Only by their own decisions
Only by their family background
By their economic situation

questions.q: What is misrecognition?
questions.a: Seeing a person or group through a false or negative image
w: Treating everyone in exactly the same way
Giving people too many opportunities
Refusing to agree with someone's opinions

questions.q: Why can misrecognition be harmful?
questions.a: It can cause people to develop a negative image of themselves.
w: It can make people lose interest in politics.
It can cause people to question every social rule.
It can prevent people from learning about other cultures.

questions.q: What does it mean to internalize a negative image?
questions.a: To begin believing negative ideas about yourself
w: To understand why other people have different opinions
To refuse to listen to criticism
To change your identity to fit into a new society

questions.q: Taylor discusses the experiences of women. What problem does he identify?
questions.a: Some women began to believe that they were inferior to men.
w: Women were given too many opportunities.
Women were encouraged to become political leaders.
Women were unable to understand their own identities.

questions.q: According to Taylor, why might people struggle to use new opportunities even after social barriers are removed?
questions.a: They may have internalized negative beliefs about themselves.
w: They may not have enough education.
They may prefer traditional social hierarchies.
They may not want to compete with other people.

questions.q: What example does Taylor give concerning Black people in white society?
questions.a: Society projected negative images of them, which some began to believe.
w: They were encouraged to reject their cultural identities.
They were given more opportunities than other groups.
They were expected to adopt European traditions.

questions.q: What does Taylor say about the treatment of Indigenous and colonized people?
questions.a: Europeans often described them as inferior and uncivilized.
w: They were generally recognized as equal by European societies.
They were encouraged to preserve their identities.
They were responsible for creating negative stereotypes about Europeans.

questions.q: According to Taylor, is recognition simply a matter of good manners?
questions.a: No. It is a vital human need.
w: Yes. It means being polite to everyone.
Yes. It means avoiding disagreements with others.
No. It is only important for minority groups.

questions.q: According to the first idea in the reading, when is society happiest?
questions.a: When individuals pursue their own happiness
w: When everyone has the same opinions
When individuals sacrifice their happiness
When the government makes all decisions

questions.q: According to the second idea, when are individuals happiest?
questions.a: When they sacrifice their own happiness for society
w: When they have more money than others
When they can make decisions alone
When society has no conflicts

questions.q: What do people try to do when a conflict occurs?
questions.a: Reach an agreement
w: Avoid people with different ideas
Make everyone agree with them
Protect only their own interests

questions.q: What does reaching an agreement allow people to do?
questions.a: Live together and pursue their own happiness
w: Avoid making difficult decisions
Make everyone think in the same way
Put society's happiness above everything else

questions.q: What two concepts do people use to evaluate decisions and the decision-making process?
questions.a: Efficiency and fairness
w: Freedom and equality
Wealth and power
Happiness and independence

questions.q: Why must people cooperate in creating a public space?
questions.a: Because everyone wants to be happy
w: Because everyone has the same ideas
Because the government requires it
Because conflicts must never happen

questions.q: What two interests should people keep in mind when living in public space?
questions.a: Personal happiness and the happiness of the whole society
w: Personal wealth and political power
Individual freedom and economic growth
Family happiness and national security

questions.q: What is adolescence?
questions.a: A period of rapid change and growth between childhood and adulthood
w: A time when people become completely independent
A period when people stop growing
A period when people are treated as children by society

questions.q: In the past, how did children become members of society as adults?
questions.a: After passing through initiation rites
w: After finding a job
After becoming economically independent
After reaching age 18

questions.q: Why has adolescence become longer in modern-day Japan?
questions.a: Conditions for adulthood are complicated, and early economic independence is difficult to achieve.
w: Children spend more time in school because voting is difficult.
People are no longer expected to become adults.
The age for becoming a member of society has increased to 30.

questions.q: At what age are people recognized as adults in modern-day Japan?
What is an important purpose of adolescence?
questions.a: To make ourselves strong enough to live up to society's expectations
w: To avoid the responsibilities of society
To become economically independent as quickly as possible
To follow the ideas of our predecessors

questions.q: Why does adolescence begin at a younger age than in the past?
questions.a: Because of acceleration in human development and early sexual maturity
w: Because children start school at a younger age
Because young people become emotionally independent earlier
Because society expects children to work earlier

questions.q: What question arises when physical development happens earlier?
questions.a: Whether psychological maturity develops at the same time
w: Whether children should spend more time at school
Whether young people should become economically independent
Whether physical growth will stop earlier

questions.q: What does self-awareness make us want to do?
questions.a: Make our own decisions
w: Follow our parents' decisions
Avoid meeting new people
Stop learning new things

questions.q: What are the first and second rebellious phases?
questions.a: Assertiveness in infancy and adolescence
w: Physical growth in childhood and adulthood
Learning to speak and learning to read
Starting school and entering the workplace

questions.q: What can happen during an adolescent crisis?
questions.a: We can lose sight of who we are.
w: We can become completely independent.
We can stop experiencing emotional changes.
We can understand all of society's expectations.

questions.q: What does it mean to have a stable adolescence?
questions.a: To experience no apparent crisis
w: To have no worries at all
To become independent from parents immediately
To avoid changes in our relationships

questions.q: What experiences are common during adolescence?
questions.a: Emotional changes, loneliness, anxiety, and feelings of inferiority
w: Complete confidence and emotional stability
A lack of interest in other people
Freedom from worries and frustration

questions.q: What can help us when we cannot overcome our worries alone?
questions.a: Talking to someone we trust
w: Avoiding people who have different opinions
Spending more time by ourselves
Ignoring our worries until they disappear

questions.q: What can learning adaptive behaviors help us do?
questions.a: Cope with worries and control our emotions
w: Avoid all difficult situations
Make other people agree with us
Stop experiencing frustration

questions.q: What are defense mechanisms?
questions.a: Ways of dealing with emotional problems to avoid getting hurt
w: Rules that help people become popular
Skills used to solve physical problems
Methods for avoiding all responsibilities

questions.q: According to Erik Erikson, what is the main developmental task of adolescence?
questions.a: Establishing identity
w: Becoming economically independent
Finding a permanent job
Getting married and starting a family

questions.q: What does establishing identity involve?
questions.a: Connecting different parts of ourselves, including our past, present, school, and home lives
w: Choosing one personality and never changing it
Separating our school life from our home life
Following the same values as everyone around us

questions.q: Why can't we establish our identity completely on our own?
questions.a: We need to socialize and find our place in society.
w: We need to become financially independent first.
We need to follow the expectations of our parents.
We need to avoid people with different values.

questions.q: When can we become truly independent, both mentally and emotionally?
questions.a: When we have established our own identity
w: When we stop listening to our parents and teachers
When we can make all our decisions without help
When we no longer experience anxiety or frustration

questions.q: What should we try to achieve in order to live comfortably in society?
questions.a: Harmony between our pursuit of happiness and the demands of society
w: Complete freedom from society's expectations
The same goals and values as everyone else
Personal happiness without considering other people
